queries.query: Which physical or operational mechanisms limit the long-run average number of entanglement-generation attempts in a quantum network link over many time slots (for example source duty cycle, ion heating and recooling, detector recovery, or covertness against a warden), as opposed to limits within a single attempt?
("quantum network" | "entanglement generation" | "quantum repeater") + ("entanglement generation rate" | "duty cycle" | "detector dead time")
("quantum network" OR "entanglement generation" OR "quantum repeater") AND ("entanglement generation rate" OR "duty cycle" OR "detector dead time")
("quantum network link" OR slots OR warden) AND (duty OR heating OR recooling)

selection.criterion: The paper itself identifies and analyzes a physical or operational mechanism that limits the long-run average rate or number of entanglement-generation attempts in a quantum network link over many time slots, as distinct from limits within a single attempt.

columns: Duty cycle or time budget quantified

not_measured: A citation was located in its passage; whether the passage supports the claim was not checked by a person.
Search recall was not measured: works the queries never returned are unknown.
